rankingBasis: Ordered by prominence in LITT publishing and citation impact. This is a BEST-EFFORT ESTIMATE assembled from public web sources and published bibliometric analyses, NOT a programmatic citation count (OpenAlex/PubMed/Semantic Scholar/Crossref were unavailable). Placements are firmest in the top ~10 (based on senior authorship of the field's registries and landmark trials) and softer below. Only two hardNumbers are verified figures, both from the 2025 Frontiers in Neurology epilepsy-LITT bibliometric (Gross = most prolific; Kang = most cited).
note: System of record for the Physicians tab. Each physician is mapped to database.json indication keys, which powers the related-evidence cross-links. Affiliations were web-verified as of lastUpdated; affiliationConfidence 'low' marks entries whose current primary institution could not be confirmed (shown as an 'affiliation unverified' badge). Entries with "notable": true are shown outside the numbered ranking (marked with a star badge) because they are recognized figures not ranked by LITT publication volume.

physicians.name: Eric C. Leuthardt, MD, MBA
physicians.institution: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis
physicians.littFocus: Senior/lead author on the LAANTERN registry, the largest prospective multicenter LITT dataset (787-patient analysis, 2024), and senior author of the foundational Hawasli 2013 NeuroBlate glioma series. His WashU group is one of the two dominant neuro-oncology LITT programs.
representativeWorks: LAANTERN 787-patient multicenter LITT analysis (2024)
Hawasli et al., MRI-guided LITT for intracranial lesions, Neurosurgery 2013

physicians.name: Robert E. Gross, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Rutgers — Robert Wood Johnson & New Jersey Medical Schools
physicians.littFocus: Named the single most prolific author in a 2025 Frontiers in Neurology bibliometric analysis of LITT-in-epilepsy. Senior author of the landmark real-time MRI-guided SLAH series (Willie et al. 2014) that established LITT for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, and PI of the SLATE trial.
representativeWorks: Willie/Gross real-time MRI-guided SLAH for mesial TLE, Neurosurgery 2014
SLATE (Stereotactic Laser Ablation for Temporal lobe Epilepsy) trial

physicians.name: Albert H. Kim, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Washington University School of Medicine / Siteman Cancer Center
physicians.littFocus: Co-author of the foundational Hawasli 2013 NeuroBlate glioma series and a LAANTERN 787-patient co-author; a core member of the WashU tumor-LITT program alongside Leuthardt with sustained high output on glioblastoma and metastasis ablation.
representativeWorks: Hawasli et al., MRI-guided focused LITT, Neurosurgery 2013
LAANTERN multicenter analyses

physicians.name: Jon T. Willie, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: UT Health Austin / Dell Medical School, UT Austin
physicians.littFocus: First author of the pivotal SLAH series (Neurosurgery 2014), the most influential paper establishing laser amygdalohippocampotomy for mesial TLE, and a leader of the SLATE multicenter trial. Also publishes on tumor and functional LITT.
representativeWorks: Real-time MRI-guided SLAH for mesial TLE, Neurosurgery 2014
SLATE trial

physicians.name: Daniel J. Curry, MD
physicians.institution: Texas Children's Hospital / Baylor College of Medicine
physicians.littFocus: Pioneered pediatric MRgLITT: first author of the first pediatric stereotactic laser ablation series (2012) and the leading authority on LITT for hypothalamic hamartoma. Director of the Texas Children's program that produced the largest pediatric-ablation datasets.
representativeWorks: MR-guided stereotactic laser ablation in children, Epilepsy Behav 2012
Staged MRgLITT for hypothalamic hamartoma, Neurosurgery 2020

physicians.name: Alireza M. Mohammadi, MD
physicians.institution: Cleveland Clinic — Rose Ella Burkhardt Brain Tumor Center
physicians.littFocus: Cleveland Clinic LITT lead and LAANTERN investigator; co-author on the 787-patient analysis and multiple high-impact glioblastoma, radiation-necrosis, and matched-cohort survival studies. Among the most cited on upfront LITT for newly diagnosed GBM.
representativeWorks: LAANTERN multicenter analyses
Upfront LITT in newly diagnosed GBM vs biopsy-only matched cohort

physicians.name: Veronica L. Chiang, MD
physicians.institution: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
physicians.littFocus: Yale brain-metastasis/LITT leader and lead of the LAASR multicenter prospective study of laser ablation after stereotactic radiosurgery (J Neurosurg 2018) — a defining paper for LITT in post-SRS radiation necrosis — plus LAANTERN co-authorship.
representativeWorks: Laser ablation after SRS (LAASR) multicenter study, J Neurosurg 2018
LITT vs bevacizumab for radiation necrosis

physicians.name: Ricardo J. Komotar, MD
physicians.institution: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine / Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center
physicians.littFocus: Co-leads the University of Miami LITT program, one of the highest-output tumor-ablation groups, with a large body of series on brain metastases, radical ablation of radiation necrosis, and glioma.
representativeWorks: Radical LITT ablation for biopsy-proven radiation necrosis (Luther et al. 2020)
Miami brain-metastasis LITT series

physicians.name: Michael E. Ivan, MD
physicians.institution: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine / Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center
physicians.littFocus: Co-lead of the University of Miami LITT program with Komotar; senior/co-author on the group's prolific output covering radiation necrosis, brain metastases, and glioma-microenvironment mechanistic work.
representativeWorks: Miami LITT radiation-necrosis and metastasis series
Modulating the glioma microenvironment with LITT (review, 2025)

physicians.name: Andrew E. Sloan, MD, MBA
physicians.institution: Affiliation in transition — Piedmont Healthcare (Atlanta) vs. Premier Health / Wright State (Dayton)
physicians.littFocus: First author of the NeuroBlate System first-in-human Phase I trial for recurrent glioblastoma (J Neurosurg 2013), a pivotal early clinical LITT study, and a LAANTERN 787-patient co-author.
representativeWorks: NeuroBlate first-in-human Phase I trial for recurrent GBM, J Neurosurg 2013
LAANTERN multicenter analyses

physicians.institution: Cleveland Clinic — Rose Ella Burkhardt Brain Tumor Center

representativeWorks: NeuroBlate first-in-human Phase I trial for recurrent GBM, J Neurosurg 2013
Early Cleveland Clinic tumor-ablation series

physicians.name: Michael R. Sperling, MD
physicians.institution: Thomas Jefferson University — Jefferson Comprehensive Epilepsy Center
physicians.littFocus: Senior author of Kang et al., Epilepsia 2016 — a heavily cited prospective LITT-for-mesial-TLE study — and consistently ranked among the top overall epilepsy authors in bibliometric analyses. Anchors the prolific Jefferson epilepsy-LITT group.

physicians.name: Ashwini D. Sharan, MD
physicians.institution: Thomas Jefferson University
physicians.littFocus: Co-author of the influential Kang et al. 2016 Epilepsia MTLE-LITT series and a longtime leader of the Jefferson epilepsy-surgery group, contributing to the multicenter LITT literature.

Jefferson multicenter LITT targeting studies

physicians.name: Constantinos G. Hadjipanayis, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: University of Pittsburgh / UPMC
physicians.littFocus: LAANTERN 787-patient co-author and an active glioma-ablation surgeon contributing to multicenter tumor-LITT outcomes literature; also a leader in fluorescence-guided glioma surgery.

Glioma LITT outcomes studies

physicians.name: Clark C. Chen, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University / Brown University Health
physicians.littFocus: LAANTERN 787-patient co-author and prolific glioma-LITT contributor, publishing on LITT efficacy for newly diagnosed and recurrent glioblastoma.

physicians.name: Alexandre Carpentier, MD, PhD
physicians.institution: Sorbonne University / Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital (AP-HP)
physicians.littFocus: First author of the first-ever real-time MRI-guided LITT report for brain metastases (Neurosurgery 2008) — the foundational, highly cited paper that launched modern MRgLITT. Later work shifted toward focused ultrasound, so ongoing LITT volume is lower than his citation footprint.
representativeWorks: Real-time MR-guided laser thermal therapy for metastatic brain tumors, Neurosurgery 2008
Early MRgLITT technique/feasibility reports

physicians.institution: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine / Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center
